label: LOC Ceasefire Violations (2026 YTD)
contestNote: Pakistan violated ceasefire for 10+ consecutive days in early May 2026 — most intense LoC breakdown since the 2021 DGMO ceasefire agreement. No new LoC incidents reported May 10–24; ceasefire holds at Day 379 on May 24.
deltaNote: Ceasefire broken July 17-19, 2026: first major LoC firing since Operation Sindoor truce, in the Tarkundi (Rajouri) and Balakote (Poonch) sectors — 435 days of calm ended. No casualties. Separately, a July 31 terror attack killed two non-local labourers at Kulgam, the first civilian attack in the Valley since Pahalgam. NIA chargesheeted 2 men (Aug 7-8) over a Pakistan-handled plot to bomb a passenger train and stage attacks in Punjab/Delhi. Pakistan's drawn-out AJK Assembly election concluded Aug 15 with PML-N winning 25 seats to PPP's 12, after weeks of deadly JAAC reserved-seat protests JKHRO says have killed at least 89 people since June. India called the polls a 'farce' (Aug 7); Pakistan rejected the criticism. On Aug 5 (Youm-e-Istehsal), Sharif and Dar called Article 370's revocation illegal; India's MEA rebutted that Pakistan has 'no locus standi.' On Aug 7, Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey; India's MEA said Aug 11 it is 'examining implications' for national security. India's IB warned Aug 11 of an ISI-backed terror plot targeting J&K ahead of Aug 15 Independence Day, which passed off peacefully under heavy security. On Aug 14, PM Sharif called 'every single drop' of Pakistan's water a red line and threatened a 'direct' response over the IWT; India's MEA said Aug 14 there is 'no change' in its abeyance stance. Diplomatic sparring continued through the week: Pakistan quietly removed parking poles/barricades outside the Indian High Commission in Islamabad (~Aug 17); Pakistan extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft to Sept 24 (Aug 19, 16th consecutive NOTAM extension); US Ambassador Sergio Gor called J&K 'an important part of India' during his first Srinagar visit (Aug 19), prompting Pakistan to summon the US Chargé d'Affaires and lodge a strong demarche; India reciprocated Pakistan's Islamabad move by demolishing unauthorised structures outside the Pakistan High Commission in Delhi (Aug 20). Amit Shah announced Aug 17 the bust of the ISI-backed 'Shahzad Bhatti Network' — 200+ arrests across 14 states, IEDs and Pakistan Ordnance Factory-marked grenades seized — which Pakistan's FO rejected Aug 18 as a 'malicious campaign,' countering with 'state-sponsored terrorism' accusations against India (citing the Kulbhushan Jadhav case). India's MEA dismissed Pakistan's protest over Ambassador Gor's remarks Aug 21, calling Delhi's barricade removal 'proportionate action' and reaffirming J&K as 'integral and indivisible.' AJK's 12th Legislative Assembly was sworn in Aug 24 after a final reserved-seat polling round; PML-N swept the Aug 25 speaker/deputy speaker elections (Chaudhry Tariq Farooq and Ahmed Raza Qadri, both 32-13 over PPP). The AJK premiership process then hit intra-party turbulence: Nawaz Sharif dropped his original nominee, AJK PML-N President Shah Ghulam Qadir, in favour of Barrister Iftikhar Gilani on Aug 27, prompting Qadir and ex-AJK PM Raja Farooq Haider to publicly withhold support; Qadir said he would boycott the Aug 28 assembly session and invoked Sharif's own 'Vote Ko Izzat Do' slogan. The Aug 28 assembly session to elect Gilani as 17th AJK PM proceeded on schedule (nominations 9:30am, vote 2pm, oath 4pm) despite the revolt, with PML-N's 32-seat coalition against PPP's 14 sufficient to seat him; voting in seven Poonch/Sudhnoti constituencies remains unfinished. Separately, NIA's Pahalgam probe (Aug 25) alleges a unified ISI command structure coordinating LeT/JeM/Hizbul in J&K with BKI/KZF in Punjab via Telegram-based radicalisation, building on the Aug 24 Chandigarh BKI IED-plot bust (3 arrested, ~5-6kg explosives seized). Bilateral freeze remains comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT in abeyance.
